item.title: If an elder bhikkhu, Kassapa, does not delight in the training, does not praise undertaking the training, and does not encourage those bhikkhus who do…
item.description:
If an elder bhikkhu, Kassapa, does not delight in the training, does not praise undertaking the training, and does not encourage those bhikkhus who do not delight in the training, and does not genuinely and timely praise those bhikkhus who delight in the training — such an elder bhikkhu, Kassapa, I do not praise. Why is that? Because other bhikkhus might associate with that elder bhikkhu, thinking: 'The Teacher praises him.' And those who associate with him might adopt his views. And those who adopt his views would bring about their own long-term harm and suffering. Therefore, Kassapa, I do not praise such an elder bhikkhu. If a middle bhikkhu, Kassapa ... If a junior bhikkhu, Kassapa, does not delight in the training, does not praise undertaking the training, and does not encourage those bhikkhus who do not delight in the training, and does not genuinely and timely praise those bhikkhus who delight in the training — such a junior bhikkhu, Kassapa, I do not praise. Why is that? Because other bhikkhus might associate with that junior bhikkhu, thinking: 'The Teacher praises him.' And those who associate with him might adopt his views. And those who adopt his views would bring about their own long-term harm and suffering. Therefore, Kassapa, I do not praise such a junior bhikkhu.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 3.91

item.title: One whose greed, hatred, conceit, and envy have fallen away, Like a mustard seed from a needle's point — Him I call a brahmin. One…
item.description:
One whose greed, hatred, conceit, and envy have fallen away,
Like a mustard seed from a needle's point —
Him I call a brahmin.

One who speaks gentle, beneficial, and truthful words,
Who does not offend anyone —
Him I call a brahmin.

One who in this world takes nothing not given,
Whether long or short, small or large, beautiful or ugly —
Him I call a brahmin.

One who has no longings for this world or the next,
Without longings, liberated —
Him I call a brahmin.

From: Dhammapada 383-423

item.title: - What leads the world along? What torments oneself? Is there one thing To which everything is subject? - The mind leads the world along,…
item.description:
- What leads the world along?
What torments oneself?
Is there one thing
To which everything is subject?
- The mind leads the world along,
The mind torments oneself,
The mind is that one thing
To which everything is subject.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.62

item.title: Migajāla, there are mind-objects cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. If a bhikkhu delights, praises, and…
item.description:
Migajāla, there are mind-objects cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, connected with sensual desire, enticing. If a bhikkhu delights, praises, and abides with attachment to them; because he delights, praises, and abides with attachment, delight arises. With delight as condition, sensual desire is present. With sensual desire as condition, bondage is present. Bound by the bond of delight, Migajāla, that bhikkhu is called one who lives with a second. Even if he dwells in remote lodgings, in forests, in jungle groves, with little noise, little clamor, secluded from people, remote, suitable for seclusion — still he is called one who lives with a second. Why is that? Because craving, the second, has not been abandoned; therefore he is called one who lives with a second.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 35.63

item.title: There are these four kinds of persons, bhikkhus, appearing in the world. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a person does not respect virtue, does not regard…
item.description:
There are these four kinds of persons, bhikkhus, appearing in the world. What four? Here, bhikkhus, a person does not respect virtue, does not regard virtue as supreme; does not respect concentration, does not regard concentration as supreme; does not respect wisdom, does not regard wisdom as supreme. Here, bhikkhus, a person respects virtue, regards virtue as supreme; but does not respect concentration, does not regard concentration as supreme; does not respect wisdom, does not regard wisdom as supreme. Here, bhikkhus, a person respects virtue, regards virtue as supreme; respects concentration, regards concentration as supreme; but does not respect wisdom, does not regard wisdom as supreme. Here, bhikkhus, a person respects virtue, regards virtue as supreme; respects concentration, regards concentration as supreme; respects wisdom, regards wisdom as supreme. These four kinds of persons, bhikkhus, appear in the world.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.137

item.title: There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a person without serene confidence. What five? He reproaches himself; after consideration, the wise reproach him; a bad…
item.description:
There are these five dangers, bhikkhus, for a person without serene confidence. What five? He reproaches himself; after consideration, the wise reproach him; a bad reputation spreads about him; at the time of death his mind is confused; after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a plane of misery, a bad destination, a lower realm, hell. Bhikkhus, these are the five dangers for a person without serene confidence. There are these five benefits, bhikkhus, for a person with serene confidence. What five? He does not reproach himself; after consideration, the wise praise him; a good reputation spreads about him; at the time of death his mind is not confused; after death, with the breakup of the body, he is reborn in a good destination, a heavenly world. Bhikkhus, these are the five benefits for a person with serene confidence.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.217

item.title: Having known all abodes, not longing for any, That sage is truly a sage, without greed, without clinging, No longer striving, having reached the far…
item.description:
Having known all abodes, not longing for any,
That sage is truly a sage, without greed, without clinging,
No longer striving, having reached the far shore.

All-conquering, all-knowing, of perfect wisdom,
Undefiled regarding all things, abandoning all,
With craving destroyed, liberated —
The wise know that one as a sage.

Endowed with the power of wisdom, virtuous, observant,
Calm, delighting in jhāna, mindful,
Freed from all bonds, without taints —
The wise know that one as a sage.

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.12

item.title: Sāriputta, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will have peaceful faculties, peaceful minds.' Sāriputta, you should train thus. For those with peaceful faculties, Sāriputta, and…
item.description:
Sāriputta, you should train yourselves thus: 'We will have peaceful faculties, peaceful minds.' Sāriputta, you should train thus. For those with peaceful faculties, Sāriputta, and peaceful minds, their bodily action will also be peaceful, verbal action peaceful, mental action peaceful. 'We will offer a peaceful gift to our fellow celibates.' Thus, Sāriputta, you should train yourselves.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 2.36

item.title: Dhāniya: No gadflies or mosquitoes are found here, The cattle roam on the grassy meadow, They can endure the rain when it comes. So if…
item.description:
Dhāniya:
No gadflies or mosquitoes are found here,
The cattle roam on the grassy meadow,
They can endure the rain when it comes.
So if you wish, O deva of rain, let it rain!

The Blessed One:
A raft is well made, firmly bound together,
Having crossed to the far shore, having overcome the flood,
There is no further need for a raft.
So if you wish, O deva of rain, let it rain!

From: Sutta Nipāta 1.2

item.title: Walking and standing with self-control, Sitting and lying down with self-control, The bhikkhu, self-controlled, When bending and stretching his limbs. Above, across, and all around,…
item.description:
Walking and standing with self-control,
Sitting and lying down with self-control,
The bhikkhu, self-controlled,
When bending and stretching his limbs.
Above, across, and all around,
As far as the end of the world,
Regarding whatever kind of existence,
In this world,
He well observes the arising and passing
Of all aggregates.
With mind peaceful, in right conduct,
Constantly training,
Continuously, diligently,
The bhikkhu is so called.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 4.12
